title: Tim Dooley / SPLC Prediction Audit — Pre-Indictment Claims, Later Allegations, and Recovery Targets
status: specialized prediction audit; primary-source recovery incomplete
purpose: Work backward from the April 21, 2026 federal criminal indictment of the Southern Poverty Law Center and test whether Tim Dooley made materially matching statements before the event. Separate genuine pre-event statements from public prior knowledge, post-event recollection, symbolic/systemic criticism and later assistant synthesis.
epistemic_rule: An indictment contains allegations, not proven facts. A Tim statement counts as prediction evidence only if its wording and timestamp can be established before the relevant later allegation became public. General criticism of SPLC is not equivalent to predicting a criminal indictment.

anchor_events.event: In Estate of Donald A. King / Dustin Inman Society v. SPLC, the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Alabama granted SPLC summary judgment on all counts in a civil defamation dispute involving SPLC hate-group designations.
anchor_events.importance: This earlier civil case creates ambiguity whenever an early-2026 Tim conversation refers simply to 'the SPLC case.'

anchor_events.event: A federal grand jury indicted SPLC on 11 counts involving wire fraud, false statements to a federally insured bank and conspiracy to commit concealment money laundering.
anchor_events.allegations: DOJ alleged that from 2014-2023 SPLC secretly funneled more than $3 million in donated funds to individuals associated with violent extremist groups and used bank accounts tied to fictitious entities to conceal the nature/source/ownership/control of funds.

anchor_events.event: A superseding indictment added factual allegations while retaining the core charges.
anchor_events.allegations: DOJ alleged approximately $4.1 million in tax-exempt funds were used to pay informants in extremist organizations, including allegations that some recruited members or purchased material connected with Klan activity.
anchor_events.boundary: SPLC denies fraud and argues its informant program was legitimate investigative work that prevented violence and supplied information to law enforcement.

anchor_events.event: A second superseding indictment added former SPLC executive Heidi Beirich as a defendant and additional charges/allegations.

recovered_tim_evidence.source_class: prior-conversation recovery / exact user-memory statement remembered in archive work; original underlying Tim prediction not yet recovered
recovered_wording: Do you remember Tim Dooley predicting the SPLC case?
I remember Tim Dooley predicting the SPLC case.
recovered_tim_evidence.significance: If the intended referent was the April criminal indictment, this is unusually valuable because the recollection itself predates April 21 by about two months. However, a January 7 civil SPLC judgment had already occurred, so 'the SPLC case' is ambiguous and cannot yet be treated as proof of the criminal-indictment prediction.
recovered_tim_evidence.next_step: Recover the full February 18 conversation and the earlier Tim statement it referred to.

recovered_tim_evidence.recovered_wording: Now this prediction is coming true. Was it Tim Dooley or tim dole who predicted the SPLC finally getting indicted for fraud after all the banking insurrection, FBI ties, paid informants?
recovered_tim_evidence.significance: This is not prediction evidence because it follows the April 21 indictment. It is, however, a high-value recovery key because it preserves what the user remembered the earlier prediction as containing: indictment/fraud, banking, FBI ties and paid informants.
recovered_tim_evidence.next_step: Search pre-April-21 sources for each component independently rather than importing this later wording backward.

recovered_tim_evidence.assistant_synthesis_warning: The same thread later expands these ideas into claims about SPLC as a registry/listing system linked to intelligence, finance and surveillance. Those expansions must not be back-attributed to Tim unless exact Tim wording is separately recovered.
recovered_tim_evidence.why_relevant: The later indictment concerns an SPLC Intelligence Project/informant network, financial concealment and alleged payments involving extremist-group associates, while Tim's recovered thematic language links SPLC to monitoring, labels, intelligence and a wider hidden-system metaphor. The overlap is interesting but not yet a dated pre-event prediction.

public_knowability_before_april_21.fact: SPLC had long publicly operated Klanwatch/Intelligence Project and monitored extremist organizations.
public_knowability_before_april_21.implication: Predicting that SPLC had intelligence-gathering relationships with extremist milieus is low-surprise by itself.

public_knowability_before_april_21.fact: FBI Director Kash Patel publicly severed ties with SPLC on October 3, 2025.
public_knowability_before_april_21.implication: A generic 'SPLC has FBI ties' statement after that date is not hidden-information foresight.

public_knowability_before_april_21.fact: The specific April allegations concerning fictitious bank entities, detailed payment channels and the charged fraud/money-laundering theory became public with the indictment.
public_knowability_before_april_21.implication: Any clearly timestamped Tim statement naming those mechanisms before April 21 would carry much higher evidentiary weight.

strongest_recovery_targets: Exact Tim wording predicting SPLC indictment/court action before 2026-04-21.
Any pre-2026-04-21 Tim statement using fraud, donor fraud, banking, shell/fictitious accounts, laundering or concealed payments in direct relation to SPLC.
Any pre-2026-04-21 Tim statement explicitly saying SPLC paid or funded informants inside extremist/hate groups.
The full 2026-02-18 conversation to determine whether 'the SPLC case' referred to the already-decided January civil case or the later criminal case.
Any earlier public Rational_Potato post/video/stream or Great Book version naming SPLC and a future legal consequence.
Any pre-April statement distinguishing ordinary intelligence sharing from a prediction of criminal exposure.
current_conclusion: The SPLC story is potentially one of the most important prediction-recovery targets in the Tim Dooley archive because the later federal case is unusually specific: indictment, fraud theory, banks/fictitious entities, informants, extremist-group associates and FBI/IRS investigation. The archive currently proves that Tim had a broader SPLC/intelligence/classification suspicion cluster and later remembered the prediction in very specific terms, but it does not yet prove that those specific indictment mechanics were stated before April 21. The February 18 reference to 'predicting the SPLC case' is especially important but ambiguous because an unrelated SPLC civil case had already been decided on January 7. Do not promote this to a confirmed hit until the original pre-event source is recovered.
